methodology: The original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic units by identifying individual requirements, features, behaviors, and constraints. Each atomic unit is designed to be independent, self-contained, technically specific, unambiguous, and implementable as a single requirement. This ensures a granular comparison between the two information sources.
mindtraced_atomic_units: Create a 16-bit register using D flip-flops
When byte enable is asserted, corresponding byte of 'd' is written to flip-flops on positive edge of clock
When byte enable is deasserted, corresponding byte of flip-flops retains its previous value
resetn is a synchronous, active-low reset
When resetn is low, all flip-flops are reset to 0 on the positive edge of the clock
When resetn is high, reset is inactive
All D flip-flops are triggered by the positive edge of clk
Module has inputs: clk, resetn, byteena[1:0], d[15:0]
spec_atomic_units: Module has inputs: clk, resetn, byteena[1:0], d[15:0]
Output q changes only on the positive edge of clk
When resetn is low, q is reset to 0 on the positive edge of clk
When resetn is high, the lower byte of q (q[7:0]) is updated with d[7:0] on the positive edge of clk if byteena[0] is high
The upper byte of q (q[15:8]) is updated with d[15:8] on the positive edge of clk if byteena[1] is high
If a byte enable is low, the corresponding byte of q retains its previous value
resetn is a synchronous, active-low reset
The value of q at any given clock edge depends on the values of resetn, byteena, and d at the setup time before the positive edge of clk
The reset signal resetn must be asserted long enough before the rising edge of clk to ensure a reliable reset
byteena and d must be stable before the rising edge of clk to ensure correct data is captured
There is a hold time requirement after the rising edge of clk for resetn, byteena, and d
The circuit is a sequential circuit with 16 D flip-flops
The assignments to q are non-blocking, which means that the updates to different parts of q (bytes) happen concurrently within the same clock cycle
